gen-gf-turret-road-gf-sn-pro: Commanding round letters, shaped like open parentheses, take the top spot. The pen-like line of Turret Road never thins at the joins, while SN Pro lets its curves open wide beneath it, plain sans through and through.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-source-sans-3: Letters sketched with a pencil that never presses harder carry Turret Road. Source Sans 3 takes over below, its lower-bowl a left open to breathe, and that gap is what keeps the pair feeling light.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-spinnaker: Modern and commanding, Turret Road draws round forms like open parentheses. Spinnaker, a sans-serif with connected counters, would carry paragraphs smoothly, letting the eye move through without catching on tight spots.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-stick: Commanding from the first letter, Turret Road draws round forms like open parentheses with a pen-like line of constant weight. Turret Road makes the statement; Stick keeps its exits wide for light.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-suse-mono: Turret Road draws its round, commanding letters in spaghetti-like strokes that all share a single width. And SUSE Mono, a sans with generous gaps around each letter, would read steadily across many lines.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-tajawal: Turret Road holds every stem and join at the same weight, round and commanding. Tajawal, a sans-serif with a broad hooked c, then speaks in a clean, quiet voice underneath.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-tasa-explorer: Technical-pen precision: Turret Road keeps one line weight through every round, commanding letter. TASA Explorer, a sans with curves that end like lifted brush strokes, adds a friendly softness below.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-tasa-orbiter: Plain outlines, round forms, real command: Turret Road shows no modulation anywhere in its letters. But TASA Orbiter, all plain sans with unclogged small counters, would stay easy going through paragraph after paragraph.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-tomorrow: Neon-glass punch: Turret Road is round, bold, commanding. Turret Road does best at making a statement, while Tomorrow, a sans-serif with bowls open like cupped clay, does best at quiet reading.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-varta: Varta, a sans-serif with big open eyes on every e and a, sits under the round, hairline-free letters of Turret Road. Paragraphs would move along smoothly, with nothing to snag the eye.
